classification.difficultyReason: Recognise each inverse-function family and use labelled endpoints, intercepts or asymptotes to recover familiar stretches and translations; part d permits a representative horizontal scale.

content.prompt: Find a possible equation for these inverse trigonometric graphs.

spec.description: Decreasing inverse cosine graph with endpoint guides and labelled intercept.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and coordinate labels are permanent givens; equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The decreasing curve has the inverse cosine shape. Its domain $[-2,2]$ gives a horizontal stretch by factor $2$, and its range $[0,3\pi]$ gives a vertical stretch by factor $3$.

$$y=3\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}\right).$$

At $x=0$, this gives $y=\frac{3\pi}{2}$, as shown.

spec.description: Increasing inverse sine graph through the origin, with dashed endpoint guides.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and coordinate labels are permanent givens; equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The increasing curve through the origin has the inverse sine shape. Its domain $[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]$ gives a horizontal compression by factor $\tfrac12$, and its range $[-\pi,\pi]$ gives a vertical stretch by factor $2$.

$$y=2\sin^{-1}(2x).$$

spec.description: Decreasing inverse cosine graph with dashed guides at the upper endpoint and midpoint.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph and coordinate labels are permanent givens; equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The decreasing curve has the inverse cosine shape. The domain $[1,3]$ is centred at $x=2$, so translate right by $2$. The range $[0,\frac{\pi}{2}]$ gives a vertical compression by factor $\tfrac12$.

$$y=\frac12\cos^{-1}(x-2).$$

At $x=2$, this gives $y=\frac{\pi}{4}$, as shown.

spec.description: Increasing inverse tangent curve, continuation arrows, horizontal asymptotes and labelled y-intercept; no numerical x-scale.
spec.mathematics: A possible curve is y=2 arctan(x)+pi/2; asymptotes y=-pi/2 and y=3pi/2; y-intercept pi/2. Horizontal scale is unspecified.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph, asymptotes and intercept are permanent givens; equation is answer-only.

answer.worked:
The curve has the inverse tangent shape. The midpoint of the asymptotes is the vertical translation, and their separation determines the vertical stretch.

$$\begin{aligned}c&=\frac{3\pi/2+(-\pi/2)}{2}\\&=\frac{\pi}{2},\\a&=\frac{3\pi/2-(-\pi/2)}{\pi}\\&=2.\end{aligned}$$

No numerical horizontal scale is given, so one possible equation is

$$y=2\tan^{-1}x+\frac{\pi}{2}.$$
